questions.question: Describe how the sheet is prepared for the crane's working drawing, including orientation, border and title block, the conversion table and the choice of front face.
questions.expected_answer: The squared paper is turned to landscape so the tall crane and its receding depth both fit with room for dimensions; a border is drawn 10 millimetres in and a title block 30 millimetres high along the bottom with boxes for title, team, name, date, SCALE 1:2 and mm, filled in before drawing begins. A conversion table on rough paper lists every real size and its 1:2 drawing size, for example base 297 by 210 becomes 148.5 by 105 with the receding 105 halved to 52.5 in cabinet oblique, mast 350 to 175, arm 250 to 125, handle 75 to 37.5. The side view with vertical mast, arm and visible winch is the front face, drawn true, with the base depth receding at 45 degrees, and it is positioned to leave space left and below for dimensions and right for the depth.

questions.question: Explain the order in which the crane is drawn in oblique and how the mast, arm, pulley, magnet, winch and counterweight are represented, including hidden and centre lines.
questions.expected_answer: The base is drawn first and lightly as a parallelogram with a horizontal front edge and 45 degree sides, with a thin second parallelogram for its thickness. The mast position is measured from the sketch, converted and marked, and the mast drawn as a tall vertical rectangle with an oblique top, or two lines with a dashed inner line for a dowel in a tube. The arm runs from the mast top as a horizontal rectangle with its thickness, a tie string if present as a thin line, the pulley at the tip as a small circle with chain centre lines, the string as a thin line and the magnet as a nail with a coil band hanging below. The winch at the mast foot shows the drum, its axle dashed where hidden inside supports, the handle with a grip circle and the string up the mast; the cells and switch are labelled rectangles at the back of the base as counterweight. Visible edges are then darkened with a 2B pencil over faint construction lines.

questions.question: State which dimensions the crane drawing needs and where they go, how a detail view is added, and the three checks made before the drawing is finished.
questions.expected_answer: On the front face: overall height 350, arm length 250, mast position 100 from the base front edge, handle 75, nail 100, each on a thin dimension line with arrowheads touching extension lines and the real number above; base depth 210 along a 45 degree dimension line and base length 297 along the front edge; pulley and drum diameters with the diameter symbol; no dimension repeated and no lines crossing. The winch is circled and labelled A and DETAIL A is drawn in a free corner at 1:1 or 2:1 showing drum, axle, cheeks, handle, string and stop, dimensioned, with its own scale written beneath. The drawing is checked against the brief and specifications for size, reach, switch, bulb and counterweight; against the sketch for any changes, which are annotated; and against the conventions for line types, scale, units, title block and single dimensions, with a team mate reading it back as a maker.
